title: Shared payload definitions
description: Definitions referenced by the envelope and by payload schemas. This document defines nothing on its own; it exists so that no shape is written twice.

identifier.description: A NATS-subject-safe token. The normative grammar is ^[a-z0-9-]{1,63}$ and it lives in exactly one place: protocol.ParseIdentifier. This schema carries the length bound only, deliberately, so that the character class is never restated and can never drift. A consumer that validates with JSON Schema alone must still call the identifier parser.

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 UTC with exactly millisecond precision. Fixed precision is required because the timestamp is part of the canonical form that is signed.

key_id.description: base32-nopad SHA-256 of an Ed25519 public key.

actor.description: The authenticated human a saas-attested envelope acts for. The signature is the service's; this records the person.

key_actor.description: The approver identified by the signing key whose signature was verified. It is the counterpart of actor for a deployment with no user directory: there is no login to attest, no user_id, and no email, but there is the key that signed the instruction, and that key is the thing that was actually checked. A publisher fills this in from the key its verifier resolved, never from configuration and never from a value a caller supplied.

kind.description: The discriminator, and the only value it takes. It is carried so that a reader never has to infer which kind of actor it holds from which fields happen to be set. actor declares no kind and is closed, so it can never carry one: the two shapes are disjoint by construction rather than by the absence of a field.

key_id.description: The key whose Ed25519 signature over the instruction was verified before the instruction was applied. No time is recorded beside it: verification happens at the publisher, immediately before the event that carries this actor, and that event already carries occurred_at. Two records able to disagree about one instant are worse evidence than one.

on_timeout.description: What Conductor does when an interaction expires unresolved.

redacted.description: True when the redaction pass replaced secret material in a free-form field of this payload before the envelope was signed. It tells a reader that the published text is not verbatim. The count of replacements, never the matched content, is carried by a separate audit.security record.
